about: Greenstein & Pittari, LLP is a New York personal injury firm with seven offices across Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island, Yonkers and Long Island. The firm represents people injured in car, truck and motorcycle accidents, construction and workplace accidents, slip-and-falls, and cases of medical malpractice, nursing home abuse and police misconduct, always on a contingency basis, with no fees unless the case is won.

The firm places unusual emphasis on client access: attorneys visit clients in the hospital or at home, offer video consultations, commit to returning calls promptly, and provide a mobile app for tracking the status of an injury claim. Intake and representation are available in English and Spanish.

quote.text: When you're injured in an accident, you need a few things as you begin to seek compensation: answers to your questions, support while you recover, world-class legal service, and a lawyer who never forgets you're a person — not just a number.

faq.q: How much does Greenstein & Pittari charge?
faq.a: The firm works on a contingency fee: "no fees until we win your injury case." In New York that is typically 33⅓% of the recovery for most personal injury matters; medical malpractice fees follow the statutory sliding scale. Confirm the fee agreement and how case expenses are handled at your free consultation.

faq.q: Do they offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. Consultations are free and available by phone at 1-800-VICTIM2, by video, or in person at any of the seven offices. The firm also visits clients in the hospital or at home.

faq.q: Which areas of New York do they serve?
faq.a: All five boroughs plus Westchester (Yonkers) and Long Island (Uniondale). The Brooklyn, Queens, Long Island and Staten Island offices are by appointment.

faq.q: What has Law Firm Listings actually verified about this firm?
faq.a: The score and tier shown above are computed from evidence, and the scorecard names the source and date behind every sub-factor. Attorney names come from the firm’s own site and are checked against the NYS Attorney Registration database; the attorney list says how many have been confirmed. Certification additionally requires every eligibility gate to pass, and the scorecard states which are outstanding. Certification is free, earned and cannot be purchased.
